title: Rohatsu Praise and Blame
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett takes up Suzuki Roshi's teachings and the Pali Canon story of the Buddha leaving his first teacher, Alara Kalama. Nomon asks what Buddha and awakening are, then has the sitters check in with body, emotions, and thinking. Suzuki Roshi's pigs, which won't eat while watched, and his "Letters from Emptiness" chapter turn awakening into a matter of listening. When Alara Kalama praises the young Buddha as an equal and invites him to co-lead, Nomon asks how anyone works with praise and blame in sesshin. Nomon ends with the cheap concrete garden Buddha on the altar, which has grown radiant over the years just by sitting patiently.
